title: LinkNest E8 — Visual World
question: The roll assigned Workshop Pegboard: utilitarian labeled zones for categories, tagged hooks for links, tape colors for mine vs shared. Keep it, take a fused alternate, re-roll, steer, or play the category standard straight.

options.label: Workshop Pegboard
options.body: Categories are bordered zones on a perforated board; links hang as tagged items on hooks. Personal vs group sharing reads as two label-tape colors (e.g. green vs cobalt). Operate-native: scannable zones, dense but legible, no decorative noise. Light = birch board + daylight; dark = workshop after-hours with a single fluorescent edge. First viewport: home grid of labeled zones with link counts; filter chips sit like tape strips above the board. Risk: can skew industrial if typography isn't warm enough — human hand-label energy is the fix.

options.label: Split-Flap Concourse
options.lineage: Rail departure boards — fused for LinkNest
options.body: Categories become platform columns; links are live departure rows that flip when updated. Mine/shared = row lamp color (white vs amber). Home is the board at rush hour — instant scan, zero ambiguity. Strong for bilingual RTL (columns mirror). Risk: motion-heavy; must respect prefers-reduced-motion with instant swaps.

options.label: Talavera Courtyard
options.lineage: Hand-painted tin-glazed tiles — fused for LinkNest
options.body: Each category is a tile module on a courtyard wall; links are painted motifs inside. Shared group content gets a cobalt border rule; personal tiles stay cream-ground. Warm, human, distinctly non-AI. Risk: ornament density — must stay Operate-clear at small sizes.
